headline: Wall Street's AI rout tests India's six-day rally on Dhanteras

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the sixth of November, and it's Dhanteras. Here's what matters today.

First, a storm on Wall Street. Fears that a Democratic Congress will tighten the rules on artificial intelligence and data centres wiped about 2.3 trillion dollars off American stocks overnight, and Asia is falling hard this morning.

Second, India goes into this from a position of strength. The Sensex and Nifty have risen six sessions in a row, and foreign investors bought nearly 14,800 crore rupees of Indian shares on Thursday. That's their biggest single day of buying since February 2021.

Third, it's a heavy results day, with Hindalco, Siemens, Voltas and Jubilant Foodworks among the companies reporting.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Let's start with how markets closed on Thursday. It was a day of fireworks. The Nifty jumped 2.4 percent to 24,536, and the Sensex gained 2.6 percent. Over six sessions, the Sensex has added more than 6,000 points, a gain of about 8 percent. Business Standard says that puts it on course for the strongest pre-Diwali run in more than three decades.

Financial stocks led the way. Nifty Bank rose about three and a half percent to 57,847, with every one of its stocks in the green, and the financial services index climbed more than 4 percent. Brokers and fund houses had a big day too. The capital markets index rose 4 percent, and asset management stocks gained up to 7 percent. Adani Ports and Tech Mahindra hit new highs.

Now the flows. Foreign institutional investors bought about 14,796 crore rupees of Indian shares, helped by falling crude prices and a rethink after the global sell-off in AI stocks. Domestic institutions, meanwhile, sold a record amount. Keep the bigger picture in mind, though. Foreign investors were still net sellers for October as a whole, taking out about 34,843 crore rupees. And in the Samvat year now ending, they have sold a record of about 3 lakh crore rupees.

The rupee closed at 94.47 to the dollar, its strongest since the twenty-first of October. The ten-year government bond yield eased to 7.17 percent.

Today, though, expect a pullback. GIFT Nifty is pointing to a gap-down start, somewhere between 150 and 200 points lower. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see support for the Nifty at 24,300 to 24,200, and then at 24,000. On the upside, 24,800 is the first hurdle, and 25,000 the big one.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Now to IPOs and deals. The small issue from Antala Industries closed with bids for 12.2 times the shares on offer. It raised about 23 crore rupees at up to 66 rupees a share, and listing is likely next week. Gold loan company IFL Finance has received the market regulator's approval for its public issue of 3.85 crore shares.

A big one is on the horizon. Maharashtra's state power distributor is aiming for a February 2027 listing, raising more than 10,000 crore rupees. It plans to file its prospectus by December, after the state government took over 32,679 crore rupees of its debt.

Recent listings are flying. Tonbo Imaging jumped 20 percent on Thursday and is now up 119 percent from its issue price in just two weeks. And Kissht rose 8 percent after its loan book crossed 10,000 crore rupees. It now trades at double its issue price of 171 rupees.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
On to the results roundup. In pharma, it was a tough quarter. Glenmark's profit fell about 57 percent to 264 crore rupees, with revenue lower at 4,247 crore. A Glenmark subsidiary also settled with the American insurer Humana for 15 million dollars. Biocon's profit roughly halved to 41 crore rupees, though the stock still rose nearly 6 percent.

In consumer names, Godfrey Phillips saw profit drop about 38 percent to 190 crore rupees, mainly because of higher taxes, even as revenue doubled to 4,198 crore. Nykaa tripled its profit to about 101 crore rupees, but the stock slipped 2 percent as the market wanted more. Packaging maker EPL grew revenue 30 percent to 1,567 crore rupees, with profit up four and a half percent to about 111 crore.

Some strong numbers elsewhere. Physicswallah posted its highest-ever revenue of 1,242 crore rupees, and profit more than doubled to 144 crore. The shares jumped 10 percent. Solar maker Websol Energy grew profit 73 percent to 80 crore rupees. And Paras Healthcare, in its first results since listing, earned 40 crore rupees against 12 crore a year ago.

Among the big names, Moneycontrol described Titan's quarter as a strong beat and Bharti Airtel's as in line. ONGC, NTPC, Container Corporation and Petronet LNG have announced dividends of 8 rupees, 3 rupees, 1 rupee 90 paise and 7 rupees a share. Today, watch Hindalco, Siemens, Voltas, Jubilant Foodworks, Honasa Consumer, Aster DM and Blue Dart.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Now to the economy and policy. The Centre has released an advance instalment of 1.09 lakh crore rupees of tax devolution to the states for November, to help them keep up capital spending.

On interest rates, banker Uday Kotak told Business Standard he expects the Reserve Bank to raise the repo rate by another 50 to 75 basis points, and warned of prolonged risks from the Middle East.

The market regulator, SEBI, had a busy day. Domestic investors and foreign portfolio investors can now hold up to 5 million dollars in rupee currency derivatives without showing an underlying exposure. From the first of April 2027, mutual funds can net off their purchases and sales in the cash market within a scheme. And fund managers can now certify investors as accredited, with that status valid for three years.

The Budget debate on capital gains tax is heating up. Industry body FICCI wants the long-term capital gains exemption on listed shares restored, with a higher securities transaction tax to make up the revenue. SBI Research has suggested no tax on gains from holdings older than three years, and puts the cost at 40,000 to 50,000 crore rupees. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said she will consider investors' concerns on equity taxation.

There are warning signs from the farm. Rabi sowing is down 46 percent from last year, at 37.6 lakh hectares, after a 48 percent rainfall shortfall in October. On the other side, car sales hit a record and daily UPI payments touched 1 lakh crore rupees.

Also, the government is opening a special round for deepwater oil and gas blocks, and will fund up to half the cost of exploratory wells. And a senior income tax official warned that lapses in cross-border financial reporting could hurt India's sovereign rating.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Around the world, it was a brutal night. On Wall Street, the Dow fell around 1,800 points and the Nasdaq dropped roughly 5 percent, sliding into correction territory, more than 10 percent below its October record. All three major indices had their worst day since April 2025. The trigger was fear that the Democrats, now in control of both houses of Congress, will tighten oversight of AI and data centres. Chip stocks took the worst of it. The semiconductor index fell nearly 10 percent and Nvidia lost about 9 percent, with weak forecasts from Qualcomm and Arm adding to the pain. President Trump blamed the Democrats for the losses.

Asia is following. South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 8.8 percent this morning, breaking below 5,000 and triggering a 20-minute halt in trading. Samsung and SK Hynix are down more than 9 percent. Japan's Nikkei fell as much as 7 percent and is now 20 percent below its June peak, which puts it in bear market territory.

Investors ran for safety. US Treasuries rallied, the yen rose, and gold climbed above 4,100 dollars an ounce. Brent crude is around 99 dollars a barrel as traders watch the US-Iran war and fresh tanker attacks.

One note of caution for India from Bernstein's Venugopal Garre, who told Moneycontrol not to count on fatigue with the AI trade to lift Indian markets.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India–US trade deal you're following. Sources told the Economic Times that the Democrats' win won't affect the interim deal, since it doesn't need approval from Congress, though ongoing American trade investigations could still shape the final tariffs. Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative thinks the result could push President Trump to close the India deal within two months.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
And finally, your money. It's Dhanteras, so gold is on many minds. Mint reports prices are about 20 percent below this year's peak. Experts quoted by Business Standard suggest simply restoring your planned allocation to gold rather than chasing it, and being ready for near-term swings. Hitesh Jain of Yes Securities goes further. He sees gold moving into a long, cautious consolidation over the next three to five years.

A warning for anyone investing in American stocks through apps. Nearly 30 Indian investors on the platform Stockal allege losses of about 100 crore rupees after their US holdings were sold without their authorisation. And the government's cyber security agency, Cert-In, has warned banks and fintech firms of an AI-driven campaign that exploits payment systems to move money without permission.

A few quick ones. Pensioners, the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation is reminding you to submit your digital life certificate, the Jeevan Pramaan. Non-resident Indians will be able to open trading accounts fully from abroad from the third of December, under eased SEBI rules. And a consumer court has ordered an airline to pay a Delhi flyer 71,587 rupees, after it said he was late for check-in but couldn't prove it.

That's the brief for today. Watch how deep the opening dip goes as the AI rout spreads overseas, whether foreign investors keep buying, and the Hindalco and Siemens numbers later in the day. Happy Dhanteras, and have a lovely day.
